title: Raise a hinged mast with its two guy lines and peg each so the mast stands plumb
instruction: Stand the white mast up plumb using only its two blue guy lines: put each guy's ring eye on the ground peg on its own side that holds the mast plumb, then let go of both rings.
context: Telecom line installers "Participate in the construction or removal of telecommunication towers or associated support structures" (O*NET 49-9052.00). A mast-erection manual: "Erect the mast carefully by pulling guy wire 1 and lifting the mast"; "If the mast is not vertical, adjust the guy wires, and check the position of the mast again." Here each guy has a fixed length, so plumbing means choosing the right anchor peg for each.
setup: Station table, cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left). Mast: white PLA bar 2 x 2 x 22 cm, 30 g, hinged on a grey 5 x 5 x 2 cm foot at x 30, y 0 (tips sideways only, stops at +-30 deg); starts leaning 30 deg right on its stop. Yellow PLA collar 3.4 x 3.4 x 2 cm, 10 g, slides on the mast top over a 24 N/m spring. Two blue 6 mm polyester guys tied to the collar's sides: left 29.6 cm, right 26.1 cm, lying loose on the table. Each ends in a white PLA ring eye 44 x 44 x 5 mm (32 mm square hole) with a 50 mm grip bail. Six hooked pegs: black PLA posts 8 x 8 x 30 mm with a 9 mm nose at the top pointing away from the mast, at x 30, y 20/24/28 (left) and -23/-27/-31 (right).
scoring: Measured at the end (protractor or level on the mast, top photo). Score 0 if: a gripper ever touched the mast or collar; either ring is not on a peg on its own side (post through the hole); at the end a gripper is within 3 cm of a guy or ring, or both were let go under 2 s ago; the mast leaned over 8 deg from plumb at any time since both were let go. Otherwise 1.0 if it stayed within 3 deg of plumb (left ring on y 28, right on y -23), 0.5 if within 8 deg (e.g. right ring one peg out, on y -27).
reset_notes: Take both rings off the pegs, lay the mast on its right-hand stop (30 deg), and lay each guy loose: the left one from the collar down to the table left of the foot and along it to about y +14, the right one hanging from the collar and along the table to x 17, y -19, rings flat with the bail up. Nothing is randomised.
fidelity: Toy scale. Guys are 2 cm rigid segments with bending springs (no stretch, twist or plasticity); guy stretch and tensioning hardware are lumped into one spring under the collar. Each guy has a fixed length, so the anchor peg sets its length instead of a turnbuckle. Ring eyes are rigid printed rings with a grip bail; hooked pegs stand in for guy anchors. Touch is a contact check; release is judged from gripper-to-guy distance.
